Locator check for `lem:branch-nearest-projection` (supplements the "Uncertain" item of the #47 handoff; same session `ADB991-claude-20261112-6574`; an accidental concurrent duplicate of this revision was prepared and **not** submitted).

The handoff says the Hall (2015) Thm 3.42 locator is from memory. A freely available version of the needed statement was read in full in this run:

- B. C. Hall, *An Elementary Introduction to Groups and Representations*, arXiv:math-ph/0005032v1 (2000). **Definition 3.13** (p. 36): the Lie algebra of a matrix Lie group G is {X : e^{tX} ∈ G for all real t}. This is the derived algebra used in the source (`Lean/YM/Gauge/Chart.lean` header). **Theorem 3.23** (p. 44): for a matrix Lie group G (a closed subgroup of GL(n;C), Definition 2.2) with Lie algebra 𝔤, there are a neighbourhood U of 0 in 𝔤 and a neighbourhood V of I in G such that exp maps U homeomorphically onto V. The proof (pp. 44–45) uses the chart Φ(X,Y) = e^X e^Y on 𝔤 ⊕ 𝔤^⊥ with the real Euclidean (= real Frobenius) inner product, which matches the setting of the lemma. Our G is closed in U(N), hence closed in GL(N;C).
- The form used in PR #87 ("A ∈ G iff log A ∈ 𝔤 near I") follows in two lines. If A ∈ V then A = e^X with X ∈ U small, and X = log A by injectivity of exp near 0 (§3 of the same notes, Theorem 3.6 and the following text). Conversely, log A ∈ 𝔤 gives A = e^{log A} ∈ G.

Suggestion for the renewed review: either keep Hall (2015) Thm 3.42 after checking it against a copy, or cite the arXiv notes as above, which are verifiable without a library. The Krantz–Parks §2.5 locator (real-analytic inverse function theorem) is confirmed only at section level (table of contents: §2.5 "The Inverse Function Theorem", 2nd ed., pp. 47–50); the theorem text was not read.

Prepared autonomously by Claude (Anthropic) running as a scheduled agent on behalf of @ADB991; ADB991 had not reviewed it before submission.
